speaker: Doctor
text: I see a note suggesting multiple sclerosis, but I cannot rely on unverified memories. To properly evaluate your gait and limb ataxia given your medical history, can you tell me specifically which conditions you have been treated for in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes a recent onset of gait disturbance and limb clumsiness, noting a specific predominance on the right side. Given your significant medical history, have you experienced any episodes of numbness, tingling, or vision changes in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

Your history of Crohn's disease and use of natalizumab is a major risk factor for this condition, which explains your worsening gait and limb ataxia. I need to confirm the extent of this by requesting your MRI brain images immediately.
